abstract: Aladdin Ayesh, PhD, a reader in AI at De Montfort University takes a look at AI in games.

This series of mini-articles looks at the implications of the growing internet of things (IoT). Chair of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT's Working Group on the IoT, Jeremy Crump, introduces the concept.

With an increased emphasis on employability and the skills needed to excel in the online, connected workplace, the Open University is changing its Masters computing programme. Kevin Waugh, Postgraduate Programme Director for Technologies and Computing at the Open University, explains the drivers for change and goes on to outline what these changes will look like.
Brian Runciman MBCS spoke to Richard Harris, former CIO at ARM UK and Rolls Royce.

articleTitle: The Future CIO and a Vision for IT
abstract: Colin Beveridge FBCS CITP presents a crystal-clear vision of a job for the CIO that can be easily defined and quickly recognised as a key corporate function for the foreseeable future.

In May 2012 The Secretary of State commissioned Dame Fiona Caldicott to lead an independent panel of experts to review patient/client information governance in the NHS and social care in England.Ian Herbert FBCS summarises the BCS response to Caldicott 2. Although much of what follows is relevant UK-wide<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, the focus is on NHS healthcare in England.
BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, spoke to Özlem Yüce, Agile Transformation Lead at Maersk Line, about the company's agile transformation.
Andy Smith FBCS CITP, from BCS's security community of expertise (SCoE), details the security activities that the Institute is involved with.
The extracts below are taken from the BCS's eminent academic monthly, The Computer Journal, published with Oxford University Press.
The extracts below are taken from the BCS's eminent academic monthly, The Computer Journal, published with Oxford University Press.
Brian Runciman MBCS spoke to Joerg Winkelmann, Head of IBM's Center for CIO Leadership, about the aims of the centre, the challenges facing CIOs and the career goals of aspiring CIOs.

The evolution of internet enabled devices is now becoming a reality, from watches to TVs and smarter and smarter phones, the ability to infect and spread malware is exploding. Andrew Rice asks how can we protect our data whilst keeping home/remote working and mobile data safe?
John Mitchell has spotted that attacks on mobile devices are coming from a different angle.

articleTitle: Realising the Potential for information in health and care
abstract: ‘Digital health – realising the potential for information in health and care’ is the theme for this year's HC2013 organised by BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT and HIMSS (Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society) and incorporating HEALTH+IN4MATICS. The conference takes place on 16-17 April 2013 at the International Conference Centre, Birmingham.
In the first of a new series of BCS members only briefings on IT subjects, Helen Wilcox draws material from the free resources available to BCS members on service management (SM) issues.
Helen Wilcox outlines some of the resources in the member library on business intelligence.

Learning and development budgets are being cut, people are under pressure, but real and meaningful personal development is a major part of being a professional. BCS Membership Director David Evans MBCS asks, how do we reconcile this?

Each of the four Council meetings during the year has a particular focus, and July's was around the budget for 2014/15. There was also a lively debate on communication between Council and members, and an update on BCS Learning & Development Ltd.

May saw BCS Council elect a new chair and vice-chair – one a past President and the other a new council member who was first elected to the body by the professional membership last year. Dr Roger Johnson, FBCS CITP (BCS President 1992/3) returned to the Chair's seat at May's Council meeting, and Kevin Streater, FBCS CITP took up his seat as Vice-Chair.
Keith Gordon MBCS CITP, former Secretary of the BCS Data Management Specialist Group, looks at defi nitions of big data and the database models that have grown up around it.
Unusually three new games consoles were announced at this year's CES in Las Vegas in January. The trouble is, Henry Tucker MBCS doesn't think we need any of them.

Science fiction author Isaac Asimov is as famous for the laws of robotics he created in his stories as he is for the stories themselves. Jeremy Holt MBCS of Clark Holt Commercial Solicitors looks at whether these laws are practical as robots become a reality.
Jude Umeh FBCS CITP, the Institute's DRM blogger, looks at the relationship between big data, privacy and intellectual property.
Big data needs to meet small data to deliver on healthcare's challenges says Dr Justin Whatling FBCS, Chair BCS Health and Senior Director of Population Health at Cerner.
The Agile Manifesto was signed in 2001 by a group of 17 developers. They came together to articulate and define the common ground between improved ways of developing software.
Jixin Ma, from The University of Greenwich, examines the role of time in artificial intelligence.
Louise Bennett FBCS, Chair of BCS Security, looks at the opportunities and dangers of one of the implications of big data: identity discovery through data aggregation.

articleTitle: ++The Right Content ++Well Managed ++Getting Good Security Pros
abstract: The Institute publishes new reports from analyst Forrester every month. Members have access to the full text. This is an overview of recent reports.

I've managed or advised on more agile roll-outs and implementations than I care to remember. Some of them have been storming successes. Some of them have been deeply disappointing, says Paul Dolman-Darrall MBCS.
Agile isn't just a software development methodology. Lazaro Wolf MBCS from the BCS Agile Methods Specialist Group explains why agile is a useful method for a wide and diverse group of people.

Thomas Roth-Berghofer, Professor in Artificial Intelligence, Acting Head of School & Head of Research and Research Training, school of Computing and Technology, University of West London looks at reusing experience in audio mixing and gold-ore processing
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, outlines what he sees as the big security issues for 2014.
When it comes to information assurance you need to take a wide view of the issues, says Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group.

As individuals living in a rich technology and communication ecosystem we capture, encode and publish more data than ever before. This trend toward greater amounts of data is set to increase as technology is woven ever more into the fabric of our everyday lives, says Ben Banks MBCS, European Information Security Manager, RR Donnelley.

With web 2.0 tools and social media we are all creators of content as well as consumers now. Where Twitter cut that down to 140 characters, Vine cuts video down to six seconds, says Henry Tucker MBCS as he presses record.

The benefits of using agile techniques in a project are becoming more widely understood and accepted. However, most discussions about agile (whichever particular flavour you are using) focus on the engineering (and the project management of that engineering). We in IT intuitively understand why it can be better. But why can't everyone else? asks IT Director Ali Law FBCS.
When posting information online you should always assume that it is public, says Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group.

Michael Moorcock is one of Britain's best known and at times controversial sci-fi and fantasy authors. Justin Richards MBCS, recently persuaded the multiaward winning author to answer some questions on a range of topics including writing, music, science and technology.

When people hear cyber security they automatically think of IT. So when organisations hear the words cyber security breach there is often a tendency to leave it with the IT department, not only to deal with the breach but to ensure the breach doesn't happen again says Andrew Fitzmaurice, Chief Executive, Templar Executives.

Social media is a rising cultural tide; whether you are a Facebook user, a Tweeter or just have your profile on LinkedIn Piers Wilson, Head of Product Management, Tier-3 says you need to address the security risks.
BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, remains actively involved in information security. Andy Smith FBCS CITP details what the various groups have been working on, primarily in two key areas.

BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, has licensed the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET), to award Chartered IT Professional (CITP) status to its members who meet the established criteria. IET members will join those from BCS and other licensed bodies on the Register of Chartered IT Professionals.

Although the internet is an important tool for society, we still need to deal with underlying security flaws in its infrastructure in order to counteract cybercrime and other security issues says David Bird MBCS CITP.

BCS Multimedia Editor, Justin Richards, recently caught up with Justin Whatling, Chair of BCS Health, at HC2013, to talk about the Institute's involvement with the newly launched Professional Record Standards Body (PRSB) and the current state of health informatics.
David Bird MBCS CITP does a comparison of privacy protection using popular social media data exchange models

articleTitle: Food for Thought Members on the Future of Computing and IT
abstract: BCS members gave their views on the future of computing and IT in a wide-ranging LinkedIn discussion…

Justin Whatling, Chair of BCS Health, recently spoke to BCS press officer Amanda Matheson about keeping patient records safe, his top tips for individuals to look after their records and a message for medical professionals.

Fiction can be more than simply entertainment. It can show what can be, or will be. Written by New York Times bestselling author HW Coyle and BCS member Jennifer Ellis, the following may be fiction, but it is uncomfortably close to fact.

Ravi Raizada FBCS responds to the last issue's agile special with another view, asking whether SCRUM and Kanban are enough to make you agile….
Gary York, Data Security Manager at VOSA, says that when it comes to social media companies and individuals need to be prepared to deal with the many security threats that the services pose.
Adrian Geisow is a senior research manager at HP's labs in Bristol. He is in charge of the plastic electronics programme and he spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about it.

Just when it looked as though the teaching of computing in school would be cast aside, it will now be taught alongside physics, chemistry and biology. This success is down to, in no small part, efforts from BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT says Dr Bill Mitchell, Director BCS Academy of Computing.

BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, held fringe meetings at the Conservative and Labour political party conferences, designed to focus attention on cybercrime. Brian Runciman MBCS reports from the DODS write-ups.
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, thinks mobile security is about education.

The July issue of Interacting with Computers is a special commentary on scale derivation, looking at the thorny question of measuring games engagement and any potential effects on players. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.
The Institute publishes new reports from analyst Forrester every month. Members have access to the full text. This is an overview of recent reports.
Paul Owen is a PhD Student at the University of Glamorgan focusing his research on the forensic values of mobile device data and how they can be analysed more efficiently.
Helen Wilcox outlines some of the resources in the member library on software testing.
‘Our technical understanding of embedded systems is progressively moving forward, but its implications for users is not.’ Brian Runciman MBCS looks at the latest issue of Interacting with Computers.

Suranga Chandratillake FBCS is the founder of Blinkx, the video and content platform, and gave the Turing Lecture 2013. Brian Runciman MBCS spoke to him.
This month, whilst we wait for more news on Sony's new PS4 and Microsoft to announce the replacement for the Xbox 360, Henry Tucker MBCS has gone a bit old school.

In our ever connected world it can still be hard to get in contact with someone and it can be very expensive. Clinton Finch from ShoreTel explained to Henry Tucker MBCS that this is where a single number solution comes.
The extracts below are based on extracts from the BCS's eminent academic monthly, The Computer Journal, published with Oxford University Press.
BCS past President, Professor Sir Nigel Shadbolt from Southampton University spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about his current AI work, Terminators and the ethics of AI.
Adam Davison MBCS CITP asks whether big data means big governance.

As part of the government's mission to ensure Britain competes and thrives in the global race, Education Secretary Michael Gove, has set out plans to boost the teaching of computer science by training up the first generation of outstanding new teachers in this vital subject, says The Teaching Agency.

Dr Hermann Hauser from Amadeus Capital Partners and Warren East from ARM Holdings have been made Distinguished Fellows by BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT. HRH The Duke of Kent, BCS patron, presented the awards at the Institute's annual dinner which was held this year at St James's Palace.

There are many defi nitions of artificial intelligence (AI), but I often use this one: the science of mimicking human mental faculties in a computer. One of the criticisms of this definition is that it stops at human intelligence rather than superhuman intelligence, says Adrian Hopgood FBCS CITP, Pro Vice-Chancellor and Dean of the Sheffield Business School at Sheffield Hallam University.

Big data can create business value by solving emerging business challenges. However, big data also creates security challenges that need to be considered by organisations adopting or using big data techniques and technologies says Mike Small, FBCS CITP.

In our ever connected world we are relying more and more on data centres, but they use a lot of power. With this in mind, Henry Tucker MBCS went to see the self-proclaimed, greenest data centre in the world.
David Clarke MBE, Group CEO of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, writes on the need to generate growth and how doing something different could help.

articleTitle: Project Management for IT-related Projects (Second Edition)

abstract: When it comes to developing software that works in a timely fashion, the infamous story of Boo.com is a perfect example of why delivering it early and often is the way to go.

Agile is transforming the way organisations create and manage value. Its methodologies are underpinned by incremental change with development split into smaller pieces so that it can be brought to market faster and begin delivering value to the business straight away.
Gilbert Owusu MBCS CITP and Sid Shakya MBCS from BT, Research and Technology look at how AI technologies can improve workforce management.
Helen Wilcox outlines some of the resources in the member library on big data.

Last year BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, undertook a survey of CIOs, asking them what their CEOs are asking to them to do against what they think they should be doing in the business.Brian Runciman MBCS looks at the new survey for 2013 in terms of the business requirements for the year and how they compare to 2012.

Scotland is in two minds in the run-up to the 2014 independence referendum, the ‘Yes campaign stands for independence and the ‘No’ campaign says we are better together within the United Kingdom. Freelancers have a foot in both camps, says Tom Brown from the PCG.
The BCS Personal Development Plan enables you to keep track of your personal development goals and the activities you plan and complete to reach those goals.
Warfare is changing. Confiicts are no longer confined to just a geographic area as they now spill over into the online world says Robert Pritchard.

According to John Mitchell IT governance can be defined as ‘a structure of relationships and processes to direct and control the IT function in order to achieve the enterprise's goals by sustaining and extending the enterprise's strategies and objectives’.

Today, social networking websites such as LinkedIn, Facebook and Twitter have surpassed their fundamental function as a means to stay connected with colleagues, family and friends. The rapid development of these websites has also opened up new channels for companies to communicate and reach out to their business partners and customers, says Graeme Nash.
Kevin Warwick, Professor of Cybernetics at the University of Reading, spoke to BCS Multimedia Editor, Justin Richards, about his work on cybernetics and artificial intelligence.

Managing security is critical for organisations doing business in a globally networked environment, using information technology. However, countless technical advancements do not always produce a more secure environment. All kinds of human factors can greatly affect the management of security within an organisational context, says Reza Alavi MBCS.
Mike Barwise MBCS CITP looks at the role of information assurance and how it fits in with other roles within business.

There are now more people on the planet with mobile devices than those with access to running water and they are tracked and targeted with ever more sophisticated technology by those wishing to gain, legitimately or not, from the use of that profiling information. Rick Chandler asks when is something going to be done about this.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Technology Partner and Head of Eversheds LLP's Tech, Media and Telecoms Sector, discusses how you can employ a combination of awareness training and written policies to help your employees protect your organisation's confidential information and trade secrets from security threats.
When it comes to the big security issues for 2014, John Mitchell shares an astronaut's view on infrastructure procurement.
Barry G Blundell FBCS looks at 3D, referring back to glasses-free 3D Cinema 70 years ago in Russia.

One of John Mitchell's favourite films is Invasion of the Body Snatchers where the population of a town is replaced by emotionless alien duplicates. The reason that he likes it is because it raises the question, in quite a thoughtful way, of how you tell a real person from a duplicate? Which is the very problem faced by users of social media sites.

BCS members gave their views on the future of computing and IT in a wide-ranging LinkedIn discussion…already covered on p10. The conversation mutated into one on another important issue, that of the future of IT and computing education.
The November issue of Interacting with Computers assesses some of the issues surrounding government's efforts to engage with older people. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.
Martin Sadler is Director of HP's research and development lab in Bristol. He spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about future technologies and how we need to keep them relevant.

articleTitle: to Byod or … not to Byod
abstract: Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Simon and Vicky Mann from Eversheds, outline some of legal issues to consider as well as the some of the pitfalls to be avoided and obstacles to be navigated when considering the implementation of a Bring Your Own Device programme in a work organisation.

articleTitle: Formal methods in LARGE-SCALE computing systems
abstract: Saif U. R. Malik FBCS and Samee U. Khan FBCS, from the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, North Dakota State University, talk about the significance and role of formal methods in delivering reliable and correct software.

Would you give a gun to somebody who has not been trained properly? The risk would be the same as giving a computer connected to the internet to someone who has not been properly trained says Nalin Asanka Gamagedara Arachchilage MBCS at Brunel University and visiting lecturer in computing at the University of Bedfordshire.

Most businesses now routinely use virtual meeting software to enable dispersed teams to meet without the need to travel, enabling more flexible working arrangements and reducing the barriers of time and distance. With this in mind Paul D Jagger, Secretary of the BCS Learning and Development Specialist Group, examines the drivers for and the benefits of the virtual classroom.

In the 21st century, what role can internet-based communication and social media technologies play in our activities as a professional institute? Can they support virtual meetings, or make the content generated by specialist groups and branches accessible to a greater range of members? Dr. Geoff Sharman FBCS CITP chaired the Recording and Broadcasting Working Group, which was tasked with improving audiovisual approaches for member groups.

Women choose IT as a profession less often than men, and than other under-represented groups. A BCS Position Statement published in December 2012, authored by Rebecca George OBE, Chair of the BCS Policy and Public Affairs Board, discusses the issues and how the Institute would like to see this change because there are many good opportunities for women to work and flourish in IT environments.

On the 12 June the BCS Learning and Development Specialist Group, in partnership with the Worshipful Company of Information Technologists' Education and Training committee, hosted an Oxford Union style debate on the motion: ‘This house believes that academic education will never meet the skills needs of the IT profession’. Paul Jagger FBCS, Secretary of the BCS Learning and Development Specialist Group, reports on the debate itself and on the post debate discussions.

Why are computer scientists getting involved with plant biologists? Dr Hannah Dee MBCS, Aberystwyth University, Dr Andrew French, University of Nottingham and Dr Marie Neal, Aberystwyth University, answer…

The amount of data that businesses want to collect to provide services for consumers, and the amount of privacy that consumers are willing to give away seem to be in opposition. Brian Runciman MBCS discussed this with Toby Stevens, of the Security Enterprise Privacy Group, Walid Hadid, Head of Analytics at OgilvyOne and Lance Fisher, Global CIO of SThree.

Harsha Kumara Kalutarage, a doctoral student in computer security at Coventry University, Paddy Krishnan a professor of computer science at Bond University, Australia and Dr Siraj Ahmed Shaikh FBCS CITP a senior lecturer in computer science at Coventry University look at security risks in Android apps.

articleTitle: The YIN and YANG of learning and development
abstract: The organisations in which L & D practitioners work are diverse. Learning to maximise IT's benefit is important across all sectors, industries and countries and most of the people working within them. Of course, it could be argued that this is the case for other areas, such as health and safety and legal, but some of what may reasonably be part of these specialisms, such as display screen equipment and ergonomics or data protection are often also expected to be delivered as part of any IT learning. With this in mind Jooli Atkins FBCS, Chair of BCS Learning and Development Specialist Group, discusses how we can raise the profile of L & D in IT.

The role of information and technology to support individuals in adopting a healthy lifestyle, reducing their health risk or managing their long-term condition is a topic that needs to be addressed. All health systems and their governments in developed nations recognise the need to pursue a policy of behaviour change and transfer more responsibility to individuals to manage their health and wellbeing.Dr Justin Whatling, Chair of BCS Health and Dr Wai Keong Wong, a haematology registrar, provide an overview of new BCS guidance to enable the patient's information revolution.

articleTitle: Where are we with Big Data?
abstract: There have been many descriptions of big data of late – mostly metaphors or similes for ‘big’ – deluge, flood, explosion… but not only is there a lot of talk about big data, there is also a lot of data. What can we do with structured and unstructured data? Can we extract insights from it? Is ‘big data’ just a marketing puff term? Brian Runciman MBCS introduces the ITNOW big data focus.

Gus Power has been working in software development for over 15 years and won the Gordon Pask Award in 2009. He runs a software development lab, Energized Work, and has worked on projects for Sky, British Gas and City Index, as well as several start-ups including BuyaPowa and Visual Healthcare Solutions. Still hacking code on a daily basis himself, Gus also helps companies set up environments where software development and developers can thrive.

It has been several years since cloud services became a viable and cost-effective means of managing our information and IT infrastructure. There have been numerous articles and books written about the technicalities of how organisations can make best use of the cloud and of the security issues that arise. David Sutton FBCS CITP, co-author of Information Security Management Principles says that we should turn our attention back to focus on the ‘what’ and the ‘where’, rather than on the ‘how’.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Head of the TMT Sector and Partner, Liz Fitzsimons, Legal Director, and James Ruane, Associate, from international law-firm Eversheds LLP, take us through a whistle-stop tour of a couple of recent developments in the field of data protection.

articleTitle: Digital Data Capture Solutions in Health Care
abstract: Healthcare organisations and the NHS are continually looking for new ways to reduce administrative overheads and improve productivity in hospitals, which in turn would enables clinicians to spend more time on patient care rather than on fighting stacks and stacks of paper. With this in mind Martin Brindley reports on the inroads being taken to transform the NHS from a paper-based organisation to a paperless one.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Technology Partner and Head of Eversheds LLP's TMT Sector and Edward Norris, Trainee Solicitor, Eversheds LLP, discuss two new EU directives that are being introduced to help tackle cybercrime and hacking.
